description: Scoped allow and block lists (docs/governance-lists.md). Each `decode` case is one event and what a reader must make of it; each `resolve` case is what relays returned and which list is current. Secret keys 1, 2 and 3 are public test keys.
reader: Each case is read with the reader's clock at `now` and, unless the case gives `reader.root` (resolve: `query.root`), with the subject's own key as the root. A resolve result also lists `futureDated`: the ids of copies dropped for being dated more than 600 seconds ahead.

decode.name: allow-list
decode.note: An owner's guest list for one world.

decode.name: block-list
decode.note: An owner's block list for the same world: a separate event.

decode.name: empty-list
decode.note: No entries is a list that names nobody, not an unreadable one.

decode.name: identifier-with-colons-and-unicode
decode.note: A world's d may contain colons and any printable text; only the first two colons of the coordinate separate fields.

decode.name: other-kinds-of-subject
decode.note: The subject may be any addressable thing, not only kind 37300.

decode.name: name-with-a-colon
decode.note: Everything after the pubkey's colon is the name, colons included; it is never split further.

decode.name: name-with-a-space
decode.note: Spaces are part of the name.

decode.name: no-client-tag
decode.note: The client tag is never required.

decode.name: another-client-tag
decode.note: What the client tag says never matters.

decode.name: signed-by-a-given-root
decode.note: A reader given a root of one key accepts that key: here an everyday key that is not the world's own.

decode.name: signed-by-one-of-a-given-root
decode.note: A root may be up to four keys; a list signed by any of them is read.

decode.name: dated-at-the-limit
decode.note: Dated exactly 600 seconds ahead of the reader's clock: read.

decode.name: malformed-entries-skipped
decode.note: A p tag whose value is not 64 lowercase hex is skipped and counted; the rest of the list stands.

decode.name: duplicates-collapsed
decode.note: The same key twice is one entry.

decode.name: unknown-tags-ignored
decode.note: Tags outside the format are ignored, including p tags' extra fields.

decode.name: exactly-the-cap
decode.note: 2000 entries is allowed.

decode.name: unsigned
decode.note: An event without a signature is not an event.

decode.name: wrong-kind
decode.note: Only kind 30078.

decode.name: application-wide-d
decode.note: An application-wide list's d has no subject; a scoped reader refuses it.

decode.name: two-d-tags
decode.note: Exactly one d.

decode.name: uppercase-namespace
decode.note: Namespaces are lowercase [a-z0-9._-], 1 to 64 characters, starting alphanumeric.

decode.name: version-2
decode.note: Only v1 exists; a newer version is refused, never read as v1.

decode.name: event-scope
decode.note: Only user-allow and user-deny.

decode.name: kind-with-leading-zero
decode.note: The kind is decimal without leading zeros.

decode.name: kind-too-large
decode.note: A kind is at most 65535.

decode.name: uppercase-subject-pubkey
decode.note: The subject's pubkey is lowercase hex.

decode.name: control-character-in-identifier
decode.note: No control characters in the subject's identifier.

decode.name: identifier-too-long
decode.note: The subject's identifier is at most 512 bytes of UTF-8.

decode.name: empty-identifier
decode.note: The subject's identifier is not empty.

decode.name: subject-tag-differs
decode.note: The subject tag must equal the coordinate in d exactly.

decode.name: scope-tag-missing
decode.note: The scope tag is required and must equal the scope in d.

decode.name: scope-tag-differs
decode.note: A d saying allow with a scope tag saying deny is refused, not read either way.

decode.name: version-tag-missing
decode.note: The v tag is required.

decode.name: two-scope-tags
decode.note: Exactly one of each of v, scope and subject.

decode.name: signed-by-someone-else
decode.note: Only the subject's own pubkey may sign its lists.

decode.name: no-root-given
decode.note: The same everyday-key list read with no root given: the root is the world's own key, so it is refused.

decode.name: given-root-replaces-the-default
decode.note: A given root replaces the default rather than adding to it: the world's own key is not in this root.

decode.name: trailing-space-in-subject-tag
decode.note: The subject tag is compared with d character for character; no trimming.

decode.name: dated-too-far-ahead
decode.note: Read on its own, an event dated more than 600 seconds ahead is refused. When choosing among copies it is dropped instead (see resolve).

decode.name: content-not-empty
decode.note: v1 content is empty. Hidden entries would be a new version, never read by a v1 reader.

decode.name: over-the-cap
decode.note: More than 2000 p tags refuses the event; the first 2000 are not read.

decode.name: tampered-after-signing
decode.note: An entry added after signing: the id no longer matches.

decode.name: signature-from-another-event
decode.note: A real signature over a different id.

resolve.name: newest-wins
resolve.note: The newest valid copy is the list.

resolve.name: tie-goes-to-smallest-id
resolve.note: Same created_at: the lexicographically smallest id wins.

resolve.name: forged-newer-is-not-a-candidate
resolve.note: A newer event under the owner's key without the owner's signature cannot replace the list.

resolve.name: impostor-is-not-a-candidate
resolve.note: Someone else's list for the owner's world is not a candidate.

resolve.name: refused-newest-is-unreadable
resolve.note: If the owner's newest copy is refused, the list is unreadable; an older copy is not used instead.

resolve.name: other-world-not-found
resolve.note: A list for another world does not answer for this one.

resolve.name: a-list-from-the-future-does-not-stand
resolve.note: A list dated a year ahead is dropped before choosing, and reported; the current list stands.

resolve.name: a-malformed-list-from-the-future-does-not-make-it-unreadable
resolve.note: Dropped before choosing, not refused as the newest: the current list stands.

resolve.name: only-a-list-from-the-future
resolve.note: If every copy is dated too far ahead, the list is not found, and the reader says it saw them.

resolve.name: newest-across-the-given-root
resolve.note: With a root of several keys, the newest list from any of them is the list.

resolve.name: a-key-outside-the-root-is-not-a-candidate
resolve.note: The same newer list, read with no root given: only the world's own key counts.

resolve.name: nothing-returned
resolve.note: No events: not found. A reader says so; it is not an empty list.
